definition.description: Whether the bolus dose of the medication was confirmed during the initiation process.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record explicitly confirms the administration or the dose of the initial bolus.
definition.missing_value_rule: If no mention of bolus confirmation is found in the record, represent as 'Not Confirmed'.
definition.name: bolus_dose_confirmed

definition.description: The morphological characteristic of bone lesions identified in the patient record.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the described type of bone lesion morphology (e.g., lytic, blastic, or mixed) from the musculoskeletal or oncology sections of the clinical record.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no specific morphology is documented.
definition.name: bone_lesion_characteristics

definition.description: Presence of bone metastasis at the time of pretreatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Determine if there is any documentation of bone or osseous metastasis in the pretreatment record, typically extracted from radiology reports (e.g., bone scan, PET/CT, CT, MRI) or oncology assessment notes.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if bone metastasis is not mentioned or the documentation is too ambiguous to determine presence or absence.
definition.name: bone_metastasis_presence

definition.description: The anatomical location of the patient's reported or observed bone pain.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the anatomical region of the skeleton associated with reported bone pain, tenderness during physical examination, or documented symptomatic bone metastases (e.g., 'T8' or 'thoracic spine' maps to 'Thoracic spine'; 'L3', 'low back', or 'lumbar spine' maps to 'Lumbar spine'; 'femur' maps to 'Femur').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no bone pain location is documented or if bone pain is mentioned without a specified location.
definition.name: bone_pain_location

definition.description: Presence of bone pain during the pretreatment period.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract whether bone pain is documented in the pretreatment records. This includes explicit mentions of 'bone pain', 'bone discomfort', or 'back pain' when it is associated with osseous metastases (e.g., 'thoracic bone pain', 'lower-back pain radiating to the left flank', or 'right femoral pain').
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if bone pain is neither documented as present nor explicitly denied in the record.
definition.name: bone_pain_status

definition.description: Whether a booster vaccination is clinically indicated for the patient prior to treatment.
definition.measurement_definition: Identify if the patient record explicitly states that a booster vaccination is indicated or recommended based on clinical criteria.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if there is no mention of booster vaccination indication in the record.
definition.name: booster_vaccination_indication

definition.description: Presence or absence of a pathogenic mutation in the BRAF gene.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the BRAF mutation status from molecular profiling or next-generation sequencing (NGS) reports. 'Wild-type', 'no pathogenic variants', or 'no mutations identified' map to 'Wild-type'. The identification of any activating mutation (e.g., V600E) or a label of 'Mutated' maps to 'Mutated'.
definition.missing_value_rule: If the BRAF status is not documented or the documentation is ambiguous, the value is represented as null.
definition.name: braf_mutation_status

definition.description: The presence or absence of brain edema.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the status of cerebral edema from radiology reports (e.g., MRI T2 FLAIR) or neurological clinical evaluations.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if brain edema is not documented or the status is ambiguous.
definition.name: brain_edema_status

definition.description: Total number of discrete lesions identified within the brain parenchyma.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the total number of distinct, discrete intracranial lesions (such as enhancing nodules, masses, or FDG-avid foci) reported in the neuroimaging findings. If the report explicitly states 'no lesions' or 'no abnormal uptake', the value is 0.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain imaging is documented or if the report does not specify the number of lesions.
definition.name: brain_lesion_count

definition.description: The maximum diameter of the largest brain lesion.
definition.measurement_definition: Extract the largest dimension in centimeters of the largest brain lesion identified on brain MRI. If only one dimension is provided, use that value. If multiple dimensions are provided for a single lesion, extract the maximum of those values.
definition.missing_value_rule: Represent as null if no brain lesions are identified, if brain imaging was not performed, or if the size of the lesion is not specified.
definition.name: brain_lesion_size

score_meaning.univariable: minus_log10_p; support uses nominal_p; q_support recorded separately

themes.disagreements: Strong effect modification signals for mutation status and CK5/6 expression contrast with the primary confounding roles of CMP results and general enzyme elevation.
themes.interpretation: Genomic, pathological, and laboratory markers reflecting a spectrum from strong treatment-effect heterogeneity to primary confounding.
themes.name: Genomic and Pathological Biomarkers

themes.disagreements: High-magnitude signals for intracranial lesions and bone pain contrast with purely prognostic cerebral imaging or treatment-predictive anatomical attributes.
themes.interpretation: Indicators of disease location, severity, and anatomical abnormalities, manifesting as a mix of prognostic factors, confounders, and effect modifiers.
themes.name: Disease Burden and Anatomical Indicators

system:
You review pretreatment candidate measurements using modeling evidence
from one outer-training fold. First identify themes across candidates; then
reconcile their roles as confounder, effect_modifier, both, or neither.
All evidence is fallible. No individual family, p-value, or support frequency is
a hard selection gate. A credible complementary signal can justify retention
even when other methods shrink it away. Do not mistake correlated aliases or
proxies for multiple independent discoveries. Themes organize evidence; they
do not establish equivalence, merge measurements, or transfer a role to every
theme member. Preserve investigator-locked roles exactly.

Treatment prediction, outcome prognosis, and confounding are distinct. Discuss
whether a candidate could be a common cause rather than an instrument or only a
prognostic factor. Effect modification needs treatment-heterogeneity evidence;
outcome main-effect importance alone does not establish it. Univariable logistic
interactions are on the log-odds scale and unadjusted for other covariates.
Orthogonal linear models, candidate R-learners, and causal forests assess the
probability/outcome scale after elastic-net nuisance adjustment. Their targets
and biases differ. A model family is evidence, not an independent replication.

Use exposure and evaluability denominators. Missing or nonconverged fits are not
negative votes. Repeated samples and folds overlap; support fractions are not
causal probabilities or formal stability-selection error guarantees. Raw and BH
p-values do not correct the upstream adaptive discovery process. Permutation
importance can be diluted by correlated alternatives and does not prove a
causal role. Compare fold consistency, methods, subsets, and conflicting facts.
Definitions and theme names cannot establish a role without the supplied
empirical evidence. Never invent an oracle, data-generating process, or hidden
truth. Return the requested JSON and cite only supplied evidence IDs.
